skill.name: at-dispatch-v2
skill.description: Convert PyTorch AT_DISPATCH macros to AT_DISPATCH_V2 in ATen C++ code. Use it for native kernels, CUDA kernels, and operator implementations that need the newer dispatch API.
skill.summary: Guides PyTorch developers through AT_DISPATCH_V2 macro conversions in ATen C++ files.
skill.author: pytorch

security_audit.summary: All 58 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks around C++ code, macro names, paths, and code fences in SKILL.md. No shell execution, external command invocation, network access, secret access, or prompt-injection content was found. static_findings.snippet: This skill helps convert PyTorch's legacy AT_DISPATCH macros to the new AT_DISPATCH_V2 format, as de
- Working with files in `aten/src/ATen/native/` that use dispatch macros
1. **Reorder arguments**: `scalar_type` and `name` come first, then lambda, then types
2. **Wrap the lambda**: Use `AT_WRAP(lambda)` to handle internal commas
3. **Expand type groups**: Use `AT_EXPAND(AT_ALL_TYPES)` instead of implicit expansion
Add the v2 header near the existing `#include <ATen/Dispatch.h>`:
For combined patterns, use multiple `AT_EXPAND()` entries:
From `AT_DISPATCH_*_AND2(type1, type2, ...)` or `AT_DISPATCH_*_AND3(type1, type2, type3, ...)`, extr
2. **Composable type sets**: Mix and match type groups with `AT_EXPAND()`
- Keep `#include <ATen/Dispatch.h>` - other code may need it
- The `AT_WRAP()` is mandatory - prevents comma parsing issues in the lambda
- Type groups need `AT_EXPAND()`, individual types don't
- The v2 API is in `aten/src/ATen/Dispatch_v2.h` - refer to it for full docs

content.user_title: Convert PyTorch Dispatch Macros to V2
content.value_statement: PyTorch ATen code can contain older AT_DISPATCH macros that are hard to update consistently. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through structured AT_DISPATCH_V2 conversions.
actual_capabilities: Identifies common legacy AT_DISPATCH macro forms in ATen C++ files.
Maps legacy dispatch macro families to AT_DISPATCH_V2 type groups.
Reorders dispatch arguments into the AT_DISPATCH_V2 call structure.
Adds the Dispatch_v2.h include near existing Dispatch includes.
Uses AT_WRAP and AT_EXPAND patterns shown in PyTorch examples.
Handles examples with extra scalar types and multiline lambdas.
limitations: Does not compile, run, or test converted C++ code.
Focuses on ATen dispatch macros, not unrelated PyTorch refactors.
Requires the user or agent to inspect complex macro arguments carefully.
May need manual review when local formatting or macro wrappers are unusual.

use_cases.title: Modernize Native Kernels
use_cases.description: Update older ATen native C++ kernels from legacy dispatch macros to AT_DISPATCH_V2.

use_cases.title: Prepare Reviewable Refactors
use_cases.description: Create focused dispatch macro changes that reviewers can compare against existing kernel behavior.

use_cases.title: Port CUDA Dispatch Code
use_cases.description: Apply the v2 dispatch structure to CUDA kernel launch code that uses AT_DISPATCH variants.

prompt_templates.title: Convert One Macro
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner conversion of a single dispatch block.
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert the AT_DISPATCH macro in this ATen C++ snippet to AT_DISPATCH_V2. Explain the argument mapping in simple terms.

prompt_templates.title: Update A Kernel File
prompt_templates.scenario: Convert all dispatch macros in one source file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this ATen kernel file and convert each legacy AT_DISPATCH use to AT_DISPATCH_V2. Keep unrelated code unchanged.

prompt_templates.title: Handle Complex Types
prompt_templates.scenario: Convert macros that include complex and extra scalar types.
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert these dispatch macros that include complex types and individual extra types. Show which AT_EXPAND groups and trailing types you selected.

prompt_templates.title: Audit A Migration Patch
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of an existing conversion.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this AT_DISPATCH_V2 migration patch for argument order, AT_WRAP placement, AT_EXPAND usage, includes, and missed legacy macros.

output_examples.input: A kernel file uses a legacy all-types dispatch macro with extra half and bfloat16 cases.
output: The result identifies the scalar type expression, debug name, lambda body, base type group, and individual extra types.
It returns a converted AT_DISPATCH_V2 call and notes that the v2 dispatch header should be present.

output_examples.input: A patch already converted several dispatch blocks and needs review.
output: The review checks whether each lambda is wrapped, type groups are expanded, and individual types are listed plainly.
It highlights any legacy macros that remain and any include changes that still need attention.

output_examples.input: A CUDA kernel contains a multiline lambda with commas inside template calls.
output: The result preserves the lambda body and explains why wrapping the complete lambda is required.
It keeps unrelated CUDA launch logic outside the dispatch conversion.

best_practices: Convert one dispatch block at a time when the macro arguments are complex.
Keep surrounding kernel logic unchanged unless the conversion requires local formatting changes.
Review the final file for include placement, argument order, AT_WRAP, and AT_EXPAND usage.
anti_patterns: Do not remove existing Dispatch.h includes unless the whole file no longer needs them.
Do not wrap individual scalar types with AT_EXPAND.
Do not change kernel behavior while performing a mechanical dispatch migration.

faq.question: What does this skill convert?
faq.answer: It converts PyTorch legacy AT_DISPATCH macros into the newer AT_DISPATCH_V2 format for ATen C++ code.

faq.question: Does it compile or test the result?
faq.answer: No. The skill focuses on accurate source conversion and expects separate build or test validation.

faq.question: Which files is it designed for?
faq.answer: It is designed for ATen native kernels, CUDA kernels, and native operator implementations in PyTorch.

faq.question: Can it handle extra scalar types?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains how to move extra scalar types after the expanded v2 type groups.

faq.question: Why is AT_WRAP important?
faq.answer: AT_WRAP protects the lambda argument from comma parsing issues inside complex expressions or template calls.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code or Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is written for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows that edit source files.
